newsitem.title: USA: Clinton seeks $200 mln in new disaster aid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton seeks $200 mln in new disaster aid.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Tuesday said he was seeking an additional $200 million in disaster aid for the flood-ravaged states of North Dakota, South Dakota and Minnesota and said the federal government would reimburse 100 percent of the costs of immediate emergency work.

"Anyone who has been here and seen the destruction, as I have, knows that this is not an ordinary disaster, if there is such a thing," Clinton said at a roundtable discussion on the flooding. "The people here are giving 100 percent and we should too."
The president's request for an additional $200 million in aid brings the total amount of assistance that he has sought for the three states to $488 million.

Clinton, who earlier toured the region by helicopter, also said he was designating 18 counties in Minnesota and 43 counties in South Dakota eligible for federal assistance to cope with the flooding. Clinton had already declared 149 counties in the three states disaster areas.

"People ... have unbelievably dealt with blizzards, floods and fires all at the same time," Clinton told the discussion group at Grand Forks Air Force Base, where 2,500 people who have had to flee their homes are being housed temporarily.
"I don't recall ever in my life seeing anything like this and I have been very impressed by the courage and the faith that all of you have shown," Clinton said.
